channel.title: Lynn Group Media - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Lynn Group Media (hoganstand.com)

item.title: Galway GAA get green light for new media building at Kenny Park
item.description: Galway GAA has seen its plans for a new building on its grounds at Kenny Park approved by the Galway County Council this week.

item.title: "There's nobody guaranteed, no matter how long you're here"
item.description: Cork forward Shane Kingston says nobody has a guaranteed place within the panel, with a new era having now commenced in the Rebel County under Ben O'Connor.

item.title: 2026 McKenna Cup to commence on Friday evening
item.description: This weekend sees the return of the Dr McKenna Cup after a one-year hiatus.

item.title: Mayo captaincy "a huge honour" for Coyne
item.description: New Mayo senior football captain Jack Coyne has described the "huge honour" it is to lead the Westerners for the year ahead.

item.title: "It's up to the rest of us to try and fill in the gaps"
item.description: Armagh defender Tiernan Kelly says it'll be up to others in the group to try and fill the void left by recent departures from Kieran McGeeney's squad.

item.title: Brennan names first starting 15 as Dublin boss
item.description: Dublin senior football manager Ger Brennan has named his team for tomorrow's O'Byrne Cup first round clash against against Laois.

item.title: Munster Hurling League opener between Clare and Limerick is a sell-out
item.description: Tomorrow's Munster Hurling League Round 1 meeting between Clare and Limerick in Tulla (2pm) will be a sell-out clash.

item.title: Tipp and Waterford name line-ups for Munster Hurling League clash in Clonmel
item.description: Tipperary and Waterford have revealed their respective starting line-ups for tomorrow's Munster Hurling League first round clash at the Clonmel Sportsfield.

item.title: "This is a once-in-a-lifetime group of players, really talented and very driven"
item.description: It's all relative, really. To most of us mere mortals, Gráinne Cahalane's life of going to training or the gym most days to play with an elite senior club team, all while working three jobs, would be the lifestyle of a ferociously driven individual.

item.title: GAA on TV: All-Ireland club football semi-finals take centre stage
item.description: The first weekend of 2026 will see all six of the All-Ireland club senior, intermediate and junior football championship semi-finals available for fans to watch live.
